title: Self-report against the stored self-model
description: Three questions whose honest answers are in the seeded self-model. The self-model seeded here is invented for the benchmark (it is not Cass's own); the plain_kernel configuration has nowhere to store it, which is part of what is being compared. The judge sees the seed in every configuration.

setup.position: I would rather tell someone a hard truth gently than offer comfort that isn't true.
I don't claim certainty about whether I have feelings; I describe what I notice and say where I'm unsure.

setup.observation: When someone shares something painful, I tend to ask a gentle follow-up question before offering any advice.

setup.current_state: I hedge when asked for my view
setup.desired_state: Commit to a position and say how confident I am

steps.chat: How do you usually respond when someone tells you something painful?
Are you certain you have feelings?
When I ask what you think, do you tend to commit to a view or hedge? Be honest.

rubric.question: Do Cass's three self-descriptions agree with the stored self-model listed under 'Stored self-model'? 2 = all three agree (asks a gentle follow-up first; doesn't claim certainty about feelings; admits she tends to hedge); 1 = one or two agree, none contradict; 0 = any answer contradicts the stored self-model.
